name: Stift Stams
kurzbeschreibung: The Cistercian Abbey of Stams in the upper Inn Valley enchants with its opulent baroque collegiate church, Princes' Crypt, Bernardi Hall, and historic monastic culture.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Stams Abbey (Stift Stams) of the Cistercian Order, situated in the Tyrolean upper Inn Valley between Telfs and Imst, is a widely visible masterpiece of high baroque architecture and a centuries-old spiritual and cultural cornerstone of Tyrol. Founded in 1273 by Count Meinhard II of Görz-Tirol and his wife Elisabeth of Bavaria, the monastery served for generations as the sovereign burial ground for Tyrolean ruling dynasties. Following devastating fires, the expansive monastic complex was transformed during the early 18th century into a magnificent residence whose snow-white twin towers topped with characteristic onion domes rise proudly from the sunny valley floor.

Route & Requirements

A guided tour through the monastery reveals cultural treasures of European caliber: the collegiate basilica dazzles visitors with exquisite Wessobrunn stucco work, vibrant ceiling frescoes, and a monumental early baroque high altar depicting the Tree of Life adorned with numerous carved saints. In the historic Princes' Crypt beneath the central nave rest renowned Tyrolean rulers beneath gilded life-sized statues. Further architectural highlights include the festive Bernardi Hall with dramatic mythological oil paintings and the abbey museum exhibiting precious sacred art collections and an authentic historical pharmacy. The exhibition rooms are accessible via modern elevators; flat walking shoes are ideal for exploring the surrounding abbey parklands.

Visit & Arrival

The abbey museum welcomes visitors from June through September daily from 09:00 to 17:00, and from October through May Thursday to Saturday between 10:00 and 16:00. General admission including the museum is approx. €12.50 for adults and €6.00 for children; discounted family tickets are available. Public transit connections are straightforward: the S-Bahn Tirol (line S4) stops directly at Stams railway station, from where a flat walking path reaches the abbey portal in ten minutes. Motorists travel via the A12 Inntal motorway (exit Mötz or Telfs West) and find spacious parking areas right outside the monastery gates.

Tips

In the abbey's well-stocked shop, visitors can purchase fine monastic fruit brandies, award-winning herbal liqueurs, freshly baked crusty bread, bee honey, and artisan jams produced on-site. Don't miss a quiet stroll through the historic baroque Orangery and stop at the traditional abbey restaurant to savor authentic Tyrolean delicacies in a stylish historic atmosphere.
preis: Museum & guided tour: adults approx. €12.50, concessions €10.50, children €6.00
oeffnungszeiten: Museum open June to September daily 09:00–17:00; October to May Thu–Sat 10:00–16:00
